50+ regional DSD partners; national coverage expected within 12-15 months, eliminating out-of-stocks at Target, CVS and other retailers.
Europe/Nordics revenue grew ~70% on new flavors; new lower-caffeine 'tropics' line launched.
China restructured into royalty model recouping the $12.2M prior investment; H1 net income $10.2M heavily aided by ~$12M one-time China note gain.

North America flavors, powder packs, nootropics
Other sizes/flavors for North America, color on powder packs and expected uptick, plans to bring more flavors like nootropics to North America.

Flavor innovation brings retailer excitement; innovation team plans additional SKUs and rationalization (Kiwi Guava #1 in many accounts). Powders saw strong online/fitness-channel gains, smoothie usage via influencers. Nootropics line - lower-caffeine, initially in 7-Eleven - has planned back-half launch into new verticals.
Any studies or clinical work being conducted in any geography.
No active studies currently underway, but always explores studies when developing new lines/innovation, consistent with science-based positioning.
Seasonality for upcoming quarter/back half and reminder of 2018 Q2/Q3 dynamics and bigger-picture trends.

Trends strong (SPINS +38.6%), category shifting to better-for-you. Summer beverage-season seasonality affects baseline business but offset by new retailer listings. Flagged $1.2M of NA revenue shifted from Q2 2018 to Q3 2018 on production timing.
What is driving Celsius's improved shelf space and recent highlights.

Transformation in energy category - traditional brands (Full Throttle, NOS, Rockstar) declining per SPINS, consumers want healthier options. Cited Monster CEO Rodney Sacks's commentary that brands like Celsius gain shelf space. Numerous 2020 category-review meetings; category shift also why premier DSD partners take on Celsius.
DSD network build-out and second-half impact
Which DSD regions remain to be covered and where the biggest second-half impact from added DSDs should come.

Biggest coverage in Southeast; filling voids for full coverage to flip retailers (7-Eleven, CVS, Target) from warehouse to DSD, gaining ACV and in-stock execution. Coverage includes Southeast, Texas, Michigan, NY, New England, California, Vegas; ~50 premier partners, continuing to expand.
Potential to expand into other European regions and how the company approaches growth in newer EU regions.

Lot of European opportunity but focus on profitable growth. Next phase activates Finland and Norway (marquee retailer listings expected) and further Nordic penetration; Spain and Germany under discussion - but want the expansion model correct.
Whether elevated marketing spend (Tough Mudder events) continues or grows in the back half, and which events/areas drove the increase.

Goal is profitable growth; reinvesting incremental gross profit/EBITDA into marketing and sales. Hired sales reps to manage DSD; investing in verticals like food service. Spend went to Tough Mudder activation, guerilla/demo sampling, online advertising. Q3 active but staying near breakeven.
What end customers and new accounts could move the needle this year and next.

Significant opportunity within existing roster via optimization (dry shelf -> cold cooler -> front-checkout, citing Sprouts). Target room for more SKUs/cold; CVS national rollout complete with SKU/front-checkout room; Rite Aid green-lit for energy door. New targets: Walgreens, Duane Reade, Speedway; convenience ACV only 10.9% - lots of runway.
Whether there is an opportunity for a CBD-based recovery drink and, if so, the timeline.

Innovation team looking at adjacent categories; CBD in development for some time, a CBD product is ready in the portfolio. Watching regulatory process, want any launch to leverage existing routes to market - no definitive timeline but will be ready.
